notes.note: Re-recorded after merging main's #3081. session-api.md now holds both #3081's passage on how a request closes when its turn is aborted and #2932 part 2's passage on the structured Claude ask reason and the chained-Bash gaps, in separate paragraphs of the respondToRequest section. The ADR cites the session API only as the current orchestration surface; neither passage touches its decisions.

Re-recorded on the bytes merged with main's #3081 (settle requests when their turn is aborted); this record took main's bindings in the merge and the earlier #2932 part 2 notes remain in the notes files. Two changes to claude-adapter.ts meet here. #3081: interruptTurn cancels requests raised during the SDK interrupt before publishing turn.aborted, and a main-thread request.opened names its turn in turnId. #2932 part 2: the adapter owns the engine spawn, reads each ask's structured reason from the engine's stdout by request_id, publishes it as claudeAsk and treats a missing record as an escalation. They do not interact: a pending request's ask record is consumed when canUseTool takes it, before the request is opened, so the abort settlement finds nothing of part 2's to clean up, and request.opened carries both turnId and claudeAsk. Checked the page against the merged source: the structured-reason section (reason types, classifier_approvable, decision_reason_code, every PowerShell ask, the Bash-only plain chain, the fail-closed missing record, the tap bounds, replay only on the initialize response) and the three chained-Bash gaps with their captured fixture still match claudeAskEscalates and the adapter tests, which pass on the merged tree alongside #3081's new stop-gap tests. The page makes no claim about turn-abort settlement, so #3081 changes nothing it states.
